speaker: Poet (derivation)
question: Whose is all this?
premises: From your waking, his waking; from your sleep, his rest.
Hence all is of your nature: the world as real-unreal.
inference: Waking and sleep derived: his waking yours, his rest yours — hence all is of your nature, real-and-unreal.

speaker: Poet (exhaustion)
question: What use are rites for the formless?
premises: The tongue is tired in your name; the mind is tired in remembering you.
Of the formless, what meditation; of the qualityless, what name.
inference: Rites exhausted at the start: tired tongue, tired mind — meditation with no form to hold, name with no quality to name.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: Where is the seat for the all-based?
premises: Where is summoning for the full; where a seat for the all-based.
Foot-water and respects for the clean; sipping for the pure.
inference: The kutaḥ series opens: summoning, seating, washing, sipping — each rite asked where, for whom without place.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What bath, garment, scent, jewel?
premises: What bath for the stainless; what garment for the world-bellied.
What scent for the unanointed; what jewel for the lovely.
inference: Adornment rites interrogated: no bath, no garment, no scent, no jewel where stainless, world-full, unanointed, lovely.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What thread, flowers, incense, lamp?
premises: Sacred thread for the propless; flowers for the desireless.
Incense for the noseless, lamp for the eyeless — what use.
inference: Offering rites interrogated: thread, flowers, incense, lamp — each without a receiver.
uncertainties: Print variant apraṇasya (for-breathless) noted; edition aghrāṇa (noseless) kept.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What offering, circumambulation, obeisance?
premises: Food-offering for the ever-content, betel for the Lord — whence.
Circumambulation for the endless, obeisance for the non-dual — whence.
inference: Honorific rites interrogated: food, betel, circling, bowing — all without a needy recipient.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: How is the hymn enjoined?
premises: Whence waving-lights for the self-shining Lord.
How is a hymn enjoined for the Veda-unspeakable.
inference: Even praise interrogated: lights for the self-shining, hymn for the unspeakable — enjoined how.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: How sending-off, how oblation?
premises: How is sending-off for the full, inside and out.
And how is oblation for the difference-free, everywhere.
inference: Farewell and fire-offering interrogated: no going out for the full, no difference for the fire.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What fee, libation, dismissal, pardon?
premises: Where is the fee for the full; libation for the ever-content.
Dismissal for the all-pervading; pardon for the unseen.
inference: Closing rites interrogated: fee, drink, dismissal, pardon — none owed where full, content, everywhere, unseen.

speaker: Poet (seal)
question: What then is worship?
premises: Just so, indeed, the highest worship, in all states, always.
With nondual mind, yoke the mind to God as Lord of all.
inference: The answer after twenty negations: nondual mind yoked to the Lord of all, in every state, always — that is the highest worship.
